conceptual assets.concept: Control bus (ctrl) — execution control and CSR access signals (including pc_ret and csr_* fields)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The control bus is produced by the control unit and consumed across execution and CSR flows: control outputs drive the internal signal `ctrl` (neorv32_cpu_control_inst: ctrl_o => ctrl) and other sub-blocks read it (neorv32_cpu_regfile_inst: ctrl_i => ctrl; neorv32_cpu_icc_inst maps `ctrl.csr_we`, `ctrl.csr_re`, `ctrl.csr_addr`, `ctrl.csr_wdata`). The write-back selection uses `ctrl.pc_ret` in `rf_wdata <= alu_res or lsu_rdata or csr_rdata or ctrl.pc_ret;`. These RTL relations show control fields determine register writebacks and CSR operations; their integrity is required for correct execution and CSR behavior.

conceptual assets.concept: Register-file write-back value (rf_wdata) — data supplied to the register file for architectural writes
conceptual assets.reasoning: The write-back value is computed in this entity and delivered to the register file: `rf_wdata <= alu_res or lsu_rdata or csr_rdata or ctrl.pc_ret;` and the regfile instance receives it as `rd_i => rf_wdata` (neorv32_cpu_regfile_inst). The register-file writes (architectural state updates) depend on rf_wdata; the RTL establishes that corrupting this value changes register contents, so Integrity is required.

conceptual assets.concept: Register-file read outputs (rs1, rs2, rs3) — general-purpose register contents used by execution units
conceptual assets.reasoning: The regfile drives `rs1`, `rs2`, `rs3` (neorv32_cpu_regfile_inst: rs1_o => rs1, rs2_o => rs2, rs3_o => rs3) and these signals are consumed by the ALU and control (neorv32_cpu_alu_inst rs1_i/rs2_i/rs3_i => rs1/rs2/rs3). The RTL shows these signals carry architectural register contents into execution; corrupting them violates computation correctness, establishing Integrity.

conceptual assets.concept: CSR readback result (xcsr_res) — CSR data assembled from multiple CSR sources
conceptual assets.reasoning: CSR readback is assembled in `xcsr_res` (`xcsr_res <= xcsr_cnt or xcsr_alu or xcsr_pmp or xcsr_icc;`) and supplied to the control unit (`neorv32_cpu_control_inst: xcsr_rdata_i => xcsr_res`). The RTL shows xcsr_res is the value used for CSR reads; corruption of these CSR read results would change CSR-visible behavior, establishing Integrity.

conceptual assets.concept: Aggregated machine interrupt vector (irq_machine) — combined machine interrupt inputs used by control
conceptual assets.reasoning: The aggregated interrupt vector is computed as `irq_machine <= mti_i & mei_i & msi_i;` and passed to control (`neorv32_cpu_control_inst: irq_machine_i => irq_machine`). The control unit's interrupt handling depends on this vector; the RTL shows this dependency, so integrity of the aggregated interrupt signals is established.

conceptual assets.concept: PMP fault indicator (pmp_fault) — memory protection fault reported to control
conceptual assets.reasoning: The PMP block drives `pmp_fault` (neorv32_cpu_pmp_inst: fault_o => pmp_fault) and the control unit reads it (neorv32_cpu_control_inst: pmp_fault_i => pmp_fault). The RTL shows control decisions depend on this fault signal for memory-protection handling; corrupting it would alter exception behavior, establishing Integrity.

conceptual assets.concept: LSU exception indicators and fault address (lsu_err, lsu_mar) — memory-access error information consumed by control
conceptual assets.reasoning: The LSU provides error and fault-address outputs (`neorv32_cpu_lsu_inst: err_o => lsu_err, mar_o => lsu_mar`) and the control unit receives them (`neorv32_cpu_control_inst: lsu_err_i => lsu_err, lsu_mar_i => lsu_mar`). These RTL connections show control's exception handling depends on these values; their integrity is required to report and handle memory faults correctly.
